# Original qmatch source and evidence coupling

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz) and [index](index.json) preserve original
sources, actual diagnostics, separate repairs, exact source/import byte maps
and observers as text. The archive includes the preceding finite/Raw/nominal
sector and quantum-header studies; it neither extracts nor executes history.
The index binds every complete member, and the archive was read back to verify
all sizes and hashes without execution. Final current checks are recorded
separately in [validation](validation.json).

The first `SourceSector` prototype accepts a changed original arm function
while retaining free implementation indices. Its failed runtime assertion is
a real counterexample in an unexposed component. The repair proposes actual
function-evidence indices, derives implementation programs from those entries
and includes the evidence subjects in one fresh graph. Original resolved names,
source bytes, complete inputs, actual dependency snapshots and exact main/U/CU
equations remain bound together. Changing a resolved function cannot retain
the same evidence table and index under the generic checked binding theorem.

Twenty-two small runtime observations include correct canonical phase order,
an independent valid schedule and rejection of source/entry/body/phase/control
substitutions, missing evidence, unused graph nodes and unused source rows.
Two actual controlled/main phase mutations reach the exact equation refusal;
changes leaving an unrelated node instead fail graph coverage. These are runtime
observations, separately from the generic kernel-checked composition theorems
and four small original-identity reductions.

The first full-computation kernel examples hit the existing recursion depth;
a diagnostic reduction also reaches the existing heartbeat limit. Those failed
attempts stay unchanged. The limits are not raised, and the failed examples
are not presented as proofs. Shared generic fresh-receipt/input/source coupling
proofs avoid repeated whole-source evaluation. The smaller identity reductions
retain their stated scope; they do not prove concrete complete source execution.

Other retained failures include absent import products in early observer runs,
reserved identifiers, missing equality instances, incorrect offsets, proof
elaboration and unused-simplification warnings. They remain failed observations.
Primary import products are hash-bound, not freshly replayed by these component
checks. No native mode, source execution handle, QDV route, whole-source body
preservation, external schema, new guarantee or Issue completion is established.
Selector/target expression typing, general/selected quantum nominal execution,
the twelve-bit qmatch profile and #64/#195 remain unfinished. The two protected
QLV1 scopes and all pending QS/PR/RS/EXACT obligations remain unchanged.

The separate [operand history](operands-first.tar.xz),
[index](operands-index.json) and [current checks](operands-validation.json)
retain seven source-name/frame counterexamples, the equal-type zero-width owner
substitution and the public Observe sharpening counterexample. All arise in
unexposed components. Correct direct and tuple-aliased sources stay separate
from malformed sources; the escaped local name reaches an unsupported-prefix
barrier and is not evidence of general block-scope checking.

Original structural parameter/move checking repairs those cases. The first
compiled audit rejects a generated partial recursive helper; a library-fold
repair and exact `take_cons`/declarative `Move` proofs preserve the name-transfer
rule. Twelve small kernel reductions cover zero-width moves, grouping versus
singleton tuples, atomic quantum product owners, wildcard/duplicate/consumed
names and simultaneous tuple bindings. Thirty-four runtime observations retain
separate scopes from the generic proofs and complete kernel Tests.
Arbitrary calls, allocation, control flow, full source-to-Raw mapping and native
execution remain unfinished; no component or barrier closes #64/#195.
